headline: NEW to scans -- Trump says more Iran strikes before the midterms are possible, but a deal is also possible, walking back his own
dek: Asked how far he is from a possible attack on Iran, Trump said 'Do you really think I'm going to tell you if I'm going to do it? And there's a possibility I will.
sources: Times of Israel liveblog entry, reporting Donald Trump's remarks to reporters
fault_line: Is Trump keeping his no-strike-before-midterms pledge, or is the pledge already dead?

sections.what_happened: Asked how far he is from a possible attack on Iran, Trump said 'Do you really think I'm going to tell you if I'm going to do it? And there's a possibility I will. There's also a possibility we'll have a nice, big, beautiful agreement.' He added Iran wants a deal 'but the problem is, will they hold the deal?' In the same item, Iranian President Pezeshkian said on state TV that the supreme leader instructed officials to 'go and finish [the deal]' but that Washington 'broke the rules of the game' after talks were disrupted.
sections.what_verified: 1 distinct publisher family (Times of Israel T3) for this exact quote in-window; the quote's substance matches Trump's Oct 23 Florida rally line ('We may do another little Epic Fury') but the walk-back of his own Oct 8 pledge is ToI-only in-window.
sections.what_disputed: Trump's own Oct 8 Truth Social post: the US 'will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the Midterm Elections' (Nov 3); White House spokesperson Anna Kelly told ABC News Oct 23 the US would not attack before the elections; WSJ Oct 24 reported Trump leaning toward resumed strikes but no final decision. The new remark contradicts the pledge without announcing any decision.
sections.why_matters: The pledge vs the threat: Trump just reopened the door he himself closed on Oct 8 -- what changed in 16 days, and what does Pezeshkian's 'finish the deal' reply reveal about the other side's clock?
